what: chat + search-lessons run with verify_jwt=false and spend LOVABLE_API_KEY credits on every call. Added a per-caller-IP cap of 20 requests/hour, counted in public.ai_rate_limits via the atomic RPC ai_rate_limit_hit.

deploy.path: Lovable (the only deploy path for this project)

measurements.call: POST /functions/v1/search-lessons, no apikey and no Authorization header
measurements.meaning: any caller who knows the URL could spend the AI key without limit

measurements.result: 200, and the live function wrote row bucket='search-lessons:<caller ip>' hits=1
measurements.meaning: the counter is written by production, not by the test

measurements.setup: counter for this caller set to 20 (the cap) for both buckets
measurements.result: 429 on both, Retry-After: 3600, body {"error":"יותר מדי בקשות מהכתובת הזו. נסו שוב בעוד שעה."}
measurements.meaning: the cap refuses before the AI gateway is called, so a blocked request costs nothing

measurements.result: 200 on both, real streamed answers (1720 and 2998 bytes)
measurements.meaning: the public feature still works for a visitor who is not logged in

not_measured: The 21st through 20th-per-hour boundary was not walked one call at a time — that would have spent 20 real AI calls. The counter itself was proven to increment and to flip allowed=false at the limit directly against the RPC (hits 1,2,3 against p_limit=2), and the 429 branch was proven end-to-end against production.

Rate limiting is per IP, so callers behind one NAT share a bucket and a caller with many IPs can still spread load. It caps the wallet against the cheap attack, it is not an identity check — system 21 has no customer login surface today (see #172 pattern).
fail_open: If the RPC errors the request is allowed and the failure is logged. A counter outage must not take a live public chat down.
test_mode: No charge, no message sent, no account created. Only rate-counter rows were written and they were deleted.
